blocks.heading: ## The rules this list is kept under
blocks.text: **clean_room** — Every item is a CLEAN-ROOM adaptation. What is imported is the PROPERTY described in the public literature - an impasse is an occasion for learning, evidence must carry its lineage, a budget has priority and durability. No rival source is read, vendored, translated or paraphrased into this repo, and no rival identifier is adopted where it would carry a licence or imply provenance Aura does not have. Each module names the published description it was built from and states, in its own terms, what Aura does differently and why. This matches the discipline already in core/organism/model_validation.py (OpenWorm/sciunit) and core/cognition/impasse.py (Soar).

blocks.heading: ## The rules this list is kept under
blocks.text: **gates** — make gap-atlas (every card adjudicated, every closed card's test and caller present), make architecture-lint (organ shape rules), make cognitive-complexity (the kernel ratchet, raising it requires a stated reason), plus the existing compile, smoke, lint, writing and layering.

blocks.heading: ## The rules this list is kept under
blocks.text: **implement_to_what_aura_is** — The report prescribes rival-shaped mechanisms. Where Aura already has the property under another name, the work is to unify and prove, not to add a parallel organ. Where the rival's bar does not describe a non-human, non-embodied, single-machine actor, the entry is marked OVERSTATED and the transferable half is stated instead.

blocks.heading: ## The rules this list is kept under
blocks.text: **section_level_bars** — The second review gives ONE acceptance test per section, so 193 of its 194 cards carry a bar that belongs to the section rather than to the card. Every adjudication here addresses the card's own subject - its title and what the rival actually demonstrated, recorded as card_subject - and answers the section bar separately. Five cards where the two point in opposite directions say so explicitly: A8.9 through A8.12 and A12.15, where the card's subject is a rival's deployment result and the section bar is a property Aura can and does implement.

blocks.heading: ## The rules this list is kept under
blocks.text: **two_reports** — Two independent reviews landed on 2026-09-01: a comparative architecture atlas (220 cards, ids 001-220) and a cross-system engineering audit (194 items, ids A1.1-A13.15). They overlap heavily and disagree in places. Both are held here under one adjudication, and where an item appears twice the second entry names the first rather than duplicating the work.

blocks.heading: ## The rules this list is kept under
blocks.text: **what_closed_means** — A card is closed when the bar it names is established by a test that runs, and - where the bar is a claim about the SYSTEM rather than about a module - by a production caller that imports the module. Neither of those is the same as the capability being demonstrated at scale. Nine campaigns are built and have not been run: the developmental grown-versus-reset campaign, the capability board against the bare cortex, the baseline portfolio, the environment bench, continual metrics, the retrieval latency law, world-model calibration, replication on other hardware, and the red-team trend. tools/evidence_report.py names each one and what it would establish, and the claim ladder holds four claims at CAUSAL and none at USEFUL, asserted by a test. The reviews' central finding was that the architecture is ahead of its evidence; this work builds the machinery that measures the gap and does not close it.

blocks.heading: ## W6 — The scientific substrate (32/32)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[001] Human reaction-time prediction** — _ACT-R_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: ACT-R treats latency as part of the cognitive theory and fits model behavior to human timing.
  - Bar: A held-out latency/error prediction beats a candidate-count-only baseline on Aura's own recall traces.
  - Plan: Aura is not a human-subject lab. Transferable half is an Aura-native latency law fitted to her own retrieval work, registered with provenance.
  - Note: The margin over candidate count is small because the two predictors are collinear here: this recall path scans every entry once per query word, so embedding_calls is query length times candidates. What the law adds over the baseline is that interaction.
  - Closed by: `core/science/retrieval_latency.py`, `tests/test_scientific_substrate.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 800 real recalls through core.memory.hybrid_store's retrieve over stores of 200 to 2,400 entries, timed on a monotonic clock. The fitted law explains 90.5% of the variance on 560 training recalls and, on 240 it never saw, predicts with an RMSE of 0.000324s against 0.000347s for candidate count alone - 6.4% better - and 0.001379s for predicting the mean. Doubling the candidate count moves the prediction up, which is the direction that would refute it if it were wrong (docs/evidence/retrieval_latency.json)

- [x] **[035] Controlled concurrent task competition** — _NARS_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: NARS continuously allocates finite processor time among concurrent tasks according to dynamic priority.
  - Bar: Adaptive allocation beats static frequencies at equal compute.
  - Plan: Aura's loops are operationally scheduled. Value-per-compute scheduling over the W7 budget.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/cognitive_cost.py`, `tests/test_cost_budget_and_neuro.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 200 tasks, 24 units to every arm, 6 methods with returns unknown at the start. Adaptive allocation through ValueOfComputation reaches 87.7% of an oracle that knew the returns; a fixed rotation reaches 60.0% and a blind commitment 59.8%. Adaptive beats the rotation on 195 of 200 and the commitment on 146 of 200 - the commitment gets lucky about one time in six, which is the shape a real comparison has (docs/evidence/allocation_campaign.json)

- [x] **[039] Budget inheritance for derived tasks** — _NARS_ · `ABSENT`
  - What the rival showed: NARS assigns new inference tasks budgets based on truth/complexity/premises.
  - Bar: Search keeps high-value branches better than fixed depth at equal compute.
  - Plan: Derive child budgets from parent value, uncertainty, complexity and information gain (W7).
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/cognitive_cost.py`, `tests/test_cost_budget_and_neuro.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 200 searches, 40 expansions to every arm, 8 branches whose payoff saturates with depth so digging is not free. Value-guided search reaches 92.5% of an oracle that knew the best branch; fixed depth reaches 65.6%, opening all 8 to depth 5. Guided wins 194 of 200 and reaches a median depth of 33 on the branch that was paying (docs/evidence/allocation_campaign.json)

blocks.heading: ## W9 — Developmental and environmental evidence (90/90)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[026] Lifetime procedural scaling** — _Soar_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: Soar has decades of experience with chunk utility and production growth.
  - Bar: Latency and memory stay bounded over millions of firings while useful old procedures survive.
  - Plan: ChunkStore.prune already implements the EV retraction. Run the accelerated lifetime with distribution shift against the W5 registry.
  - Closed by: `core/science/continual_metrics.py`, `tests/test_developmental_science.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 2,000,000 firings over 64 compiled rules. Latency bounded: 502k firings/s. Memory bounded: peak 102MB and 192 live procedures, flat across the run. Useful old procedures survive: 64 of 64 kept in the steady-world arm, while all 64 retired in the shifted arm at a median of 7,999 firings, avoiding 812,908 wrong firings against the unaudited control (docs/evidence/procedure_lifetime.json)

blocks.heading: ## W9 — Developmental and environmental evidence (90/90)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[072] Systematic developmental curriculum** — _LIDA_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: LIDA explicitly assumes a developmental learning period.
  - Bar: Older Aura outperforms reset Aura on later stages because of prior structure.
  - Plan: The decisive experiment (184). Staged curriculum spanning perception, causality, social, skill, metacognition, representation.
  - Closed by: `core/science/developmental_campaign.py`, `tests/test_developmental_science.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 10 blocks, 60 tasks each, three arms on every task at identical context. The grown-minus-reset gap rises from 0.000 to 0.200 with a slope of +0.01444 and a bootstrap interval of [0.0059, 0.0232] that excludes zero. 0% of answers had been seen in an earlier block and the arms had the same context, so neither confound voids it. Lesioning the acquired library at evaluation erases the gap, which is what makes it prior structure rather than a correlation (docs/evidence/developmental_campaign.json)

blocks.heading: ## W9 — Developmental and environmental evidence (90/90)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[101] Attention economy integrated with graph-scale inference** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: ECAN treats attention as an economic allocation over a large knowledge graph.
  - Bar: At equal compute, attention-gated inference beats scan, random and top-degree baselines on held-out graph reasoning.
  - Plan: STI/LTI exist without scale evidence. Stress-test allocation, rent, spreading and forgetting on a large learned graph.
  - Note: Negative result kept: on a graph where relevance IS the community, plain traversal from the seeds is at least as good as the attention economy at equal touches. What ECAN buys over the walk on this benchmark is not recall.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/attention_policy.py`, `tests/test_environment_and_world.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 200k-atom community graph, 40 paired trials at a 64-read budget, matched on atom touches. The card's three baselines: ECAN reaches 83.8% of the achievable ceiling against 2.8% top-degree, 2.7% random, 2.5% scan, and wins 40 of 40 paired trials against top-degree. A fourth arm the card does not name BEATS IT: breadth-first from the same seeds spending the same 160,532 touches reaches 87.4%, and ECAN wins only 11 of 40 with 10 ties. The stated bar is met and the stronger null is not, and the evidence carries both (docs/evidence/ecan_stress.json)

blocks.heading: ## W9 — Developmental and environmental evidence (90/90)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[133] Visual temporal continuity** — _SIMA 2_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: Game agents continuously consume frame sequences and learn dynamics from visual change.
  - Bar: Moving objects stay continuously tracked and prediction beats sparse snapshots.
  - Plan: Video-rate feature stream with adaptive compression into the world model.
  - Closed by: `core/science/environment_bench.py`, `tests/test_environment_and_world.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 200 frame sequences at an equal read budget of 10 frames to each arm. Carrying a track across consecutive frames and predicting one step ahead gives a mean error of 0.357 against 2.306 for a snapshot of the same span - 84.5% better, winning 200 of 200. Through an occluder the object stays one track where a snapshot sees two things. Running it found two defects: the tracker matched on where a thing was last seen rather than where it was going, and a best-match distance of zero was read as ambiguous, so associations were refused on the best possible evidence (docs/evidence/tracking_campaign.json)
  - Still to run: the video-rate half - driving this from a real screen at frame rate rather than from synthesised sequences - needs the live display and the resident model

blocks.text:
- [x] **[140] Latent prediction instead of pixel reconstruction** — _V-JEPA 2 / large predictive world-model research_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: JEPA predicts abstract representations, avoiding spending capacity on unpredictable pixel detail.
  - Bar: A latent predictor beats the reconstruction objective on downstream planning at equal compute.
  - Plan: The VRNN reconstructs observation vectors and folds reconstruction error into surprise. Add a latent-target objective as a second arm and measure.
  - Closed by: `core/world_model/prediction_quality.py`, `tests/test_environment_and_world.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`
  - Campaign run: two objectives choosing a basis from the same 48-channel observations at the same capacity of 8. Reconstruction ranks by variance and buys 0 of 8 signal channels; latent prediction ranks by predictability and buys 8 of 8. Reconstruction wins its own loss (3.72 against 5.48) and scores 0.0 on control while latent prediction scores 0.970 - the objective with the better loss is the worse planner. Swept across noise: identical below scale 1.0, latent prediction ahead at and above it, never behind (docs/evidence/world_model_campaign.json)

  - What the rival showed: Soar deliberately seeks broad behavior from a small fixed kernel plus learned knowledge.
  - Bar: Releases hold or reduce cognitive kernel complexity while capability grows.
  - Plan: A process rule, enforceable: the W10 compression pass plus a kernel-size ratchet in config/ that only shrinks.
  - Closed by: `tools/cognitive_complexity.py`, `config/cognitive_complexity_baseline.json`, `core/science/organ_accounting.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`

  - What the rival showed: NARS derives many behaviors from one theory of adaptation under insufficient knowledge/resources.
  - Bar: Every major organ maps to an invariant; redundant organs become identifiable.
  - Plan: Write the meta-theory as a machine-readable organ->invariant table, checked by a gate, not as prose.
  - Closed by: `tools/cognitive_complexity.py`, `config/cognitive_complexity_baseline.json`, `core/science/organ_accounting.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

  - What the rival showed: CLARION subsystem boundaries are derived from a coherent theory.
  - Bar: Dependency complexity falls without losing capability.
  - Plan: Same work as 013/190.
  - Closed by: `tools/cognitive_complexity.py`, `config/cognitive_complexity_baseline.json`, `core/science/organ_accounting.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[089] Full self-hosting meta-language** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: Hyperon/MeTTa aims for programs, inference rules, types and metaprogramming to live in the same atom language.
  - Bar: Aura inspects, modifies and executes cognitive rules without editing Python, with rollback and governance.
  - Plan: metta.py has equality rewriting and grounded ops; reasoning semantics are Python. Move a named family of inference-control rules into MeTTa first.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[090] Multiple first-class Spaces** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: Hyperon exposes multiple Spaces with distinct storage/query semantics as a core abstraction.
  - Bar: Generic cognitive programs run unchanged over at least three heterogeneous spaces.
  - Plan: One Space API with add/remove/query/substitute/transaction/provenance/attention, adapters for AtomSpace, memory and world model.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[092] Programs as ordinary inspectable knowledge** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: Hyperon pushes executable program structure into the same representational universe as knowledge.
  - Bar: A query retrieves the complete executable lineage of a learned strategy and substitutes it structurally.
  - Plan: Procedures as graph-addressable atoms with source, evidence and utility links — follows W5 plus W1.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[095] Glocal knowledge processing** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: CogPrime stresses interaction between local pattern processes and global structures.
  - Bar: Local learning improves from global context without contaminating unrelated domains.
  - Plan: Local workers publish candidate atoms; global constraints feed back priors. The contamination half is the test.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[096] Probabilistic/evolutionary program learning tradition** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: MOSES searches program spaces while learning representations that make useful programs compact.
  - Bar: On frozen synthesis suites it finds compact programs beyond the deterministic enumerator horizon and survives transfer and ablation.
  - Plan: every_doing() is exhaustive enumeration to depth 2. Add MDL-guided stochastic search over the same operator library.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/library_compression.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[097] Learned representation-building inside program search** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: MOSES jointly changes representation/search rather than optimizing only coefficients.
  - Bar: Search complexity falls on later tasks and new abstractions are reused across independent program families.
  - Plan: Representation growth exists and is not an inner loop of program search. Wire residual structure -> proposed abstraction.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/library_compression.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[098] Large metagraph query/runtime engineering** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `SCALE`
  - What the rival showed: Hyperon is building a dedicated Rust/C/Python runtime for atom operations and module execution.
  - Bar: Million-atom workloads keep bounded query latency and crash-safe persistence.
  - Plan: A native backend is a large project with no current bottleneck evidence. Measure first (213): produce the scaling curve, then decide.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/atomspace.py`, `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/contract_health.py`, `core/cognition/growth_report.py`
  - Campaign run: 1,500,001 atoms held. Query latency bounded: point reads 0.833us p50 / 1.375us p99, flat from 15k to 1.5M (docs/evidence/atomspace_scale.json). Crash-safe persistence: AtomSpace.save/load through the write gateway's temp-then-rename, provenance included so a reload does not double-count a witness, and a truncated or foreign snapshot is refused rather than half-loaded (tests/test_gap_atlas_campaigns.py)

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[099] Language module/package ecosystem** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: Hyperon has modules, interpreter/runtime boundaries, C and Python APIs and dedicated CI around the language.
  - Bar: Learned and handwritten cognitive packages are independently versioned, loaded and rolled back.
  - Plan: Namespaces, versioned rule packages and capability declarations over metta.py.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[100] First-class nondeterministic program semantics at scale** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: MeTTa treats multiple reductions/answers as normal rather than immediately selecting one.
  - Bar: Ambiguous rules keep alternatives until evidence or action resolves them, and calibration improves.
  - Plan: The rewriter is nondeterministic; the rest of cognition collapses candidates to strings early. Carry weighted hypothesis sets.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[102] Explicit program/knowledge introspection** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: A metagraph makes the structure of rules and programs available to the same query language.
  - Bar: Metacognition identifies a failing cognitive procedure and proposes a structural repair from the graph.
  - Plan: Introspection today reads self-state, not program structure. Expose running plans and rule matches as temporary atoms.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[103] Distributed cognitive substrate direction** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `OVERSTATED`
  - What the rival showed: OpenCog/Hyperon architecture anticipates large/distributed knowledge and cognitive workloads.
  - Bar: Large graph and search workloads scale across workers without violating state ownership or auditability.
  - Plan: Aura is local-first by design and that is a stated value, not a deficit. The transferable half is bounded read-only compute workers with signed snapshots — build only if 098's scaling curve shows a real wall.
  - Note: Distribution is a rival's goal, not Aura's; sovereignty is the constraint that defines her.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/atomspace.py`, `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/contract_health.py`, `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[106] Meta-level rewrite of inference policy** — _OpenCog / CogPrime / Hyperon_ · `ABSENT`
  - What the rival showed: A self-hosting metaprogramming substrate can represent how inference itself should proceed.
  - Bar: Aura learns an inference-ordering policy, validates it, installs it and later revises it without Python modification.
  - Plan: Depends on 089 and 045.
  - Closed by: `core/knowledge/spaces.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[165] Independent replication footprint** — _Frontier foundation-model systems_ · `PROCESS`
  - What the rival showed: Widely used models are evaluated by many external groups.
  - Bar: Several independent replications reproduce key causal effects.
  - Plan: Release reproducible canaries and fixed evaluation packs. Requires 164 first.
  - Closed by: `core/science/replication_pack.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[187] Operator-semantic invention** — _Cross-system convergence_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: No compared system fully solves open-ended operator invention either, but Hyperon/MOSES/representation-building approaches highlight the missing level.
  - Bar: Aura derives a semantic operator absent from the original evaluator, solves a previously unreachable family, and later composes it into another learned operator.
  - Plan: The deepest item. Requires W10 rollback and sandbox proof first; self-extension without them is untestable self-corruption.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/operator_invention.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[188] Meta-language self-extension with rollback** — _Cross-system convergence_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: A truly self-extending language needs changes to evaluator semantics to be first-class, testable and reversible.
  - Bar: A new operator survives adversarial held-out tests and rollback restores exact prior semantics.
  - Plan: Versioned kernel extensions with effect types, resource bounds, differential tests and automatic rollback.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/operator_invention.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[190] Architecture compression / minimum sufficient mind** — _Cross-system convergence_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: ACT-R/NARS/Soar derive breadth from fewer core principles than Aura.
  - Bar: Core subsystem count and dependency entropy fall while benchmarks hold or improve.
  - Plan: Depends on 189. Merge and delete driven by behavioural equivalence.
  - Closed by: `tools/cognitive_complexity.py`, `config/cognitive_complexity_baseline.json`, `core/science/organ_accounting.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[193] Independent replication pipeline** — _Cross-system convergence_ · `PROCESS`
  - What the rival showed: The mature comparison systems have broader communities and external validation.
  - Bar: Multiple independent machines reproduce core causal effects within declared tolerance.
  - Plan: Containerised minimal reproductions with signed environment and model hashes. Requires 164.
  - Closed by: `core/science/replication_pack.py`, `tests/test_complexity_and_replication.py`
  - Wired by: `tools/evidence_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[215] Autonomous natural-language-to-RLC program induction** — _Cross-system convergence_ · `ABSENT`
  - What the rival showed: The new RLC can execute supplied typed workflows compositionally, but general reasoning requires deriving those workflows.
  - Bar: On held-out families, induced programs beat both the resident model and supplied-tool baselines with no answer leakage.
  - Plan: The module is answer-blind and receives operation literals. Induce the program from the problem and world state, verified by execution.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/operator_invention.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[216] RLC state as ongoing hidden cognitive context** — _Cross-system convergence_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: A stronger hybrid would let endogenous neural computation participate in continuing reasoning rather than only serialize an answer-bearing state.
  - Bar: Correct hidden injection improves multi-step continuation; wrong-state and projection lesions disrupt it; no answer text is present.
  - Plan: State is serialised today. Project qualified RLC state into controlled residual slots with the two lesions as controls.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/operator_invention.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:

  - What the rival showed: Anthropic explicitly relies on OS containment rather than reimplementing all security semantics in the model/application.
  - Bar: Subsystem survives only if lesion causes preregistered task loss or loss of a non-performance invariant.
  - Plan: Prefer the simpler hardened primitive. This is the W10 compression rule stated as a design principle.
  - Closed by: `tools/architecture_lint.py`, `config/architecture_lint_coverage.json`, `tests/test_event_spine.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[A10.1] Wake-sleep language growth** — _DreamCoder_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: DreamCoder alternates problem solving with extending its DSL using learned abstractions.
  - Bar: Same-budget cross-domain sealed battery: learned library must reduce description length/search and improve solve rate; lesion abstraction families.
  - Plan: A wake-sleep loop: solve, abstract, dream. Aura has all three phases and no loop that runs them as one cycle.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/wake_sleep.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:

  - What the rival showed: DreamCoder's abstraction phase finds shared substructure across solved programs, not only abstractions proposed whole during one task.
  - Bar: Compression ratio, downstream solve rate, wall time and memory across >10k solved traces, compared with current local ecology.
  - Plan: CORPUS-WIDE compression: refactor the whole library against every solved trace, not one primitive at a time. This is the biggest real gap in the second audit.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/library_compression.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:
- [x] **[A10.3] Neural search policy** — _DreamCoder_ · `PARTIAL`
  - What the rival showed: DreamCoder trains a network to guide program search in the evolving language.
  - Bar: Cold vs learned search on unseen tasks: nodes expanded, time-to-first-solution, solve rate and calibration across seeds.
  - Plan: A learned recognition model that proposes what to try, trained on real replay. The current prior is close to a no-op.
  - Closed by: `core/cognition/wake_sleep.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

  - What the rival showed: DreamCoder trains search guidance on imagined tasks generated from the current library.
  - Bar: Ablate dream vs replay vs both; require improved held-out search without more spurious abstractions or forgetting.

  - Closed by: `core/cognition/wake_sleep.py`, `tests/test_library_and_invention.py`
  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

  - What the rival showed: It mixes replay of real tasks with dreaming.
  - Bar: Ablate dream vs replay vs both; require improved held-out search without more spurious abstractions or forgetting.

  - Wired by: `core/cognition/growth_report.py`

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

  - What the rival showed: DreamCoder rediscovers vector algebra and laws such as Newton/Coulomb in its domains.

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

  - What the rival showed: Library growth trades explanation compression against library complexity.

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)

blocks.heading: ## W10 — Metaprogrammable cognition and operator invention (53/53)
blocks.text:

blocks.heading: ## The whole graph
blocks.text:
A call graph catches direct invocation. Software also couples through shared
state, queues, events, database reads and writes, files and cross-process IPC,
and two components can be causally coupled without ever calling each other. The
converse also holds: one function can call another ten thousand times and use
nothing consequential from it.

blocks.heading: ## 5. What must not change while doing this

blocks.heading: ## 5. What must not change while doing this
blocks.text:
* **Abstention.** A surface that guesses in the middle is worse than the
  pattern it replaces.

blocks.heading: ## 5. What must not change while doing this
blocks.text:
* **Fail-open.** No worker, no boundary, no vectors — the caller keeps what it
  did before.

blocks.heading: ## 5. What must not change while doing this
blocks.text:
* **Off the critical path.** Deciding costs a forward pass; a turn answers
  from what is known and queues the rest.

blocks.heading: ## 5. What must not change while doing this
blocks.text:
* **No prompt engineering.** These read activations. Nothing is written to
  steer the model, and nothing asks it to classify in words.

blocks.heading: ## 6. Nearest blocker
blocks.text: ## 6. Nearest blocker

blocks.heading: ## 6. Nearest blocker
blocks.text:
Labels. Every surface above needs more than a dozen examples before its
boundary is usable, and the receipt-teaching path is what supplies them from
live traffic. Durable storage landed 2026-08-20, so they now accumulate across
restarts; the first surface's boundary should be re-measured once it has a few
hundred.

blocks.heading: ## 6. Nearest blocker
blocks.text:
The other known blocker is per-sentence hidden states. A paraphrase is still a
first sighting because deciding one costs a forward pass the turn cannot
spend — while the model computed exactly those states to write the sentence,
and nothing keeps them.

  edit. Grok: "one_algebra heads are already the taxonomy... they are the
  instruction set."

blocks.heading: ### The five boundaries the audit found
blocks.text:
- **B2 — schema ceiling.** `Induced.read` fixes the rule shape to
  `after[i] = f(before[g(i,n)], before[h(i,n)])`. Arity two, one operation,
  value-blind addressing. No amount of word or maker invention changes it.

blocks.heading: ### The five boundaries the audit found
blocks.text:
- **B3 — two algebras (CLOSED 2026-09-01).** `one_algebra.Term` (positional) and
  `an_operation_that_generalises.Expression` (value) have separate primitives,
  separate enumerators, separate serialisers. An invention in one cannot be
  material for an invention in the other, so recursion is blocked across them.

blocks.heading: ### The five boundaries the audit found
blocks.text:
- **B4 — persistence hole.** `read_back` admits `HEADS` plus
  `{where, many, fixed, hole, through, undo, if}` and omits `over again`. Any
  maker she wrote using the one head the module says supplies a shape no
  fixed-length composition has is silently dropped at restart. Confirmed by
  execution, not by reading. ChatGPT found the same defect independently.

blocks.heading: ### The five boundaries the audit found
blocks.text:
- **B5 — M is not an object (CLOSED 2026-09-01).** `grow_at` takes a Python `make` callable.
  `growing_at_any_level` collapsed the API and kept the human meta-level.

blocks.heading: ### The five boundaries the audit found

## What the council got right, and what it missed
blocks.text: ## What the council got right, and what it missed

blocks.heading: ## What the council got right, and what it missed
blocks.text:
Right, and worth adopting: the universality ceiling as the organising theorem;
`Reach_B` as the growth quantity; the self-interpreter as the collapse
mechanism; a frozen governance root that the language may not rewrite; tiered
novelty; content-addressed artifacts with a dependency DAG; sealed post-freeze
tasks; the inline-expansion control; the equal-memory control; explicit
concession that finite memory forbids infinite strict accumulation.

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text:
The mechanism was complete and inert. A head that cannot refer to itself can
only compose what the positional algebra already composes, so 120 families out
of 120 produced a head the growth classifier called a shorter name. Every
council response reasoned about where new semantics come from; none noticed
that a candidate needs a fixed point before it can say anything the frontend
cannot, or that a fixed point is past what any shortest-first search reaches.
Fixed by giving a head itself and solving the step of a recurrence rather than
searching for it, at the cost of one more authored prior, named in the record.

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text: Missed by all seven:

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text:
1. **The necessity direction.** Every response proves that universality caps
   `E`. None proves that non-universality forces the regress. Without that, "use
   a universal substrate" is a preference; with it, it is the answer.

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text:
2. **A measurement of the substrate actually in the tree.** Grok calls the
   grammar "universal-enough"; DeepSeek could not find the file. Nobody
   established whether `one_algebra` is universal. It is not, and the witness is
   constructible.

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text:
3. **The last strict expressiveness gain.** If the current algebra is not
   universal, then moving to a universal floor is a genuine `E_{t+1} ⊋ E_t` —
   the only one there will ever be. That is a stronger and more surprising claim
   than the reach-only story everyone settled for, and it is provable.

blocks.heading: ### What the build itself found, which no response predicted
blocks.text:
4. **What to do about the schema ceiling (B2) and the two algebras (B3).**
   Every response noticed the heads. None noticed that the rule shape and the
   split between positional terms and value expressions are separate ceilings
   that survive a universal floor unless the floor absorbs both.

blocks.heading: # Autonomous developmental agency — the work, as a list
blocks.text:
The previous mandate asked whether the LANGUAGE of her future learning could be
a product of experience. It can, and
[RECURSIVE_ENDOGENOUS_EXPANSION.md](RECURSIVE_ENDOGENOUS_EXPANSION.md) is the
record. This one asks a different question, and the difference is the whole
point: not whether a better mechanism is expressible or findable, but whether
**she decides to go and find it**.

blocks.heading: ## Where this stands
blocks.text:
One claim in the suite is unsupported and is left that way on purpose:
[a_claim_pinned_at_its_ceiling.md](../artifacts/endogenous/a_claim_pinned_at_its_ceiling.md)
records a predicate registered against parameters at which its measurement
cannot move. It predates this work, it is not retired, and a suite that goes
green by retiring what it cannot support is a suite that has stopped meaning
anything.

blocks.heading: ## External Reproduction
blocks.text: An external reviewer can reproduce the release from scratch:

blocks.heading: ## External Reproduction
blocks.text:
```bash
# 1. Clone
git clone https://github.com/youngbryan97/aura.git
cd aura

# 2. Setup
make setup-prod

# 3. Validate
make doctor
make quality
make production-gate

# 4. Full proof (optional)
make final-proof

# 5. Run
make run
```
